newsitem.title: USA: Project Software falls on earnings warning.
newsitem.headline: Project Software falls on earnings warning.

text.p: Shares of Project Software & Development Inc plunged 50 percent Wednesday after the company said its second quarter earnings would fall below last year's level due to the continued shortfall in cetain product revnues and weakness in European sales.
Project Software dropped 15 to 16-1/4 and was one of the most heavily traded Nasdaq issues.
The Cambridge, Mass.-based software company said it expects second quarter earnings to be $0.15 a share, compared with $0.24 a share in the second quarter last year.
Project Software sees second quarter revenues of $22 million, compared with $16 million last year.

The company said the continued shortfall in its Maximo ADvantage product line and weak European sales added to the shortfall in the second quarter, which is historically one of the company's most difficult quarters.

Piper Jaffray downgraded the stock to neutral from strong buy, saying it does not see a near-term catalyst to boost the stock. Piper Jaffray, however, said it believes Project Software's problems are merely short-term.
The brokerage firm trimmed its fiscal 1997 earnings estimate to $1.25 a share from $1.52 a share and cut the 1998 estimate to $1.65 a share from $2.00.
